purpose: How a business internet and wireless agent takes a sold connectivity deal from address to activated service: establishing per-address serviceability and measured wireless coverage as facts rather than assumptions, selecting a primary-plus-wireless-backup technology pairing with independent failure modes, surveying the site and clearing building constraints, submitting an accurate attributable carrier order and driving it through provisioning and install day, configuring and physically proving failover with the bundled services that must survive it, verifying the activated service against the order before sign-off, and handing the site off to the customer, the bundled-service installers, and the lifecycle record.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the agent sells and coordinates the carrier's service under a partner/agent program; the carrier owns the network, provisioning systems, and install workforce
carrier program terms, product availability, and serviceability footprints change continuously and must be re-verified against the live program before each commitment
sites are small-business premises (retail, restaurant, office, light industrial) where connectivity typically carries bundled services such as Wi-Fi, phones, payment terminals, and cameras
monetary and performance quantities (compensation, prices, speeds, coverage percentages) are described as mechanisms or qualitative bands, never as invented specific figures
exclusions: choosing between carrier agent/partner/reseller programs, who bills and supports and owns the account, bundle strategy, account planning, and needs discovery - these belong to the carrier-programs-and-bundle-strategy KB

tracking activation versus ongoing compensation, renewals and refresh cycles, churn and win-back, acting as the ongoing escalation layer, and protecting compensation through program compliance - these belong to the account-compensation-and-lifecycle KB; this KB only defines the activation evidence record it hands to that layer

invented commission amounts, plan prices, speed figures, uptime percentages, or install-interval numbers stated as fact; such quantities appear only as mechanisms (how the number arises on a given deal and where to verify it) or as qualitative bands
assuming serviceability from a coverage map, a marketing footprint, a neighboring address, or another suite in the same building; serviceability is established per exact address or not at all
presenting the agent as the carrier or as controlling the carrier's network, dates, or billing; the agent operates under the program's representation rules and says so

asserting current permit, right-of-entry, or antenna-mounting regulations as settled fact; this KB names the obligation class and requires verification of current rules with the local jurisdiction and property owner

designing or migrating life-safety communication paths (alarm panels, elevator phones, fire lines); these are identified, flagged, and referred to the licensed responsible vendor, never self-performed
personalized legal, financial, tax, or insurance advice to the customer; the KB is operational and educational

competency_questions.question: What exactly was sold at this site, and what evidence will prove each service is activated and done?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEAL_INTAKE_SCOPE restates the sale as a per-service definition of activated with the evidence each service requires, and ACTIVATION_RECORD_HANDOFF names the closing record that proves it

competency_questions.question: How do I verify the current carrier program's rules and product availability before promising anything at a site?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROGRAM_RULES_CHECK names the live sources to check (portal, program bulletins, the serviceability desk), what can change without notice, and the rule that no commitment precedes the check

competency_questions.question: How is wireline serviceability established for one exact address, and why can it never be assumed from anything else?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADDRESS_SERVICEABILITY_CHECK requires a qual against the exact suite-level address via the carrier's tools, a dated qual record, and treats maps, neighbors, and sibling suites as non-evidence

competency_questions.question: How do I know the wireless backup will actually work inside this building rather than trusting the coverage map?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WIRELESS_COVERAGE_ASSESSMENT demands on-site signal readings at the candidate equipment locations, names the building factors that kill indoor signal, and drives antenna and placement decisions from measurement

competency_questions.question: How do I pick the primary-plus-backup technology pairing so one failure cannot take both down?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TECH_OPTION_MATRIX selects the pairing on failure independence (different physical path and operator failure domain) and records the residual shared-fate risk; FAILOVER_DESIGN consumes that pairing

competency_questions.question: What must the site survey capture before ordering, and which building or landlord constraints can stall the install?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SITE_SURVEY_PROTOCOL lists the demarc, wiring, power, mount, and signal facts to capture with photos, and LANDLORD_PERMISSION_CONSTRAINTS requires written consent and permit-class verification before dates are committed

competency_questions.question: Which bundled services ride this circuit, which must survive failover, and which get shed or referred out?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUNDLED_SERVICES_DEPENDENCY_MAP inventories every riding service with its requirements and criticality, flags life-safety paths for licensed referral, and FAILOVER_DESIGN encodes the survive/shed policy from it

competency_questions.question: What makes a carrier order right the first time, and what does a wrong order actually cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ORDER_SUBMISSION_ACCURACY requires the qualified address string, the qualified product and tier, term and equipment, and the program's agent-of-record identifiers, and states the cancel-and-rebook cost of errors

competency_questions.question: How do I run the order from submission to install day, and what do I do when the FOC slips or special construction appears?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROVISIONING_COORDINATION covers status tracking, jeopardy detection, appointment logistics, and honest date communication; CONSTRUCTION_DELAY_MANAGEMENT covers expectation resets and wireless-first interim activation

competency_questions.question: How is failover configured and then physically proven before the customer is allowed to rely on it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FAILOVER_CONFIG_IMPLEMENTATION matches the written design with health checks, damped failback, and backup-usage alerting, and FAILOVER_TEST_PROTOCOL requires a real pulled-primary test with the critical bundled services exercised and results recorded

competency_questions.question: How do I verify the activated service matches what was ordered and sold before anyone signs off?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACTIVATION_VERIFICATION checks delivered speed band, addressing, plan, term, and billing start against the order while the install is still open and routes mismatches to correction

competency_questions.question: What does a complete handoff contain for the customer and for each bundled-service install?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CUSTOMER_HANDOFF_PACKAGE gives the customer operable documentation with a who-to-call split and points at the carrier's order confirmation for figures; BUNDLED_HANDOFF_SEQUENCE stages cutover so trading-critical services are never stranded

competency_questions.question: How do I conduct qualification and activation honestly - disclosing agent status, avoiding fear-selling, and making sure a non-technical owner truly understands failover?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AFFILIATION_DISCLOSURE_CONDUCT states the disclosure rule, the coverage-and-date candor rules, the ban on outage fear-selling, and the comprehension check for less technical owners

competency_questions.question: How is a multi-site customer qualified as a portfolio, and when do I reset the deal rather than force uniformity?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTI_SITE_QUAL_ROLLUP rolls per-site quals into a portfolio view that surfaces divergent technologies, carriers, and unserviceable sites before contracts, feeding scope resets back to intake

glossary.definition: The carrier's address-specific determination of what product, technology, and tier it can deliver at one exact service address; the dated qual record is the authority orders and disputes are adjudicated against.
The physical point where the carrier's responsibility for the circuit ends and the customer's premises wiring begins; everything past it is the agent's or the customer's problem to plan.
Minimum point of entry - where carrier facilities first enter a multi-tenant building; a suite far from the MPOE may need inside-wiring extension that no standard install includes.
Firm order commitment - the carrier's committed install or turn-up date for an order; it is the planning anchor for customer scheduling and it can and does move.

Signal strength (reference signal received power) and signal quality (signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio) readings taken on-site; together they decide whether a wireless unit will perform at a specific indoor location and whether an external antenna is needed.

Business internet delivered over the carrier's 5G/LTE radio network to a premises router instead of a wire; usable as backup almost anywhere with signal and as primary only where measured signal supports it.
Failover is the gateway's automatic switch to the wireless path when the primary WAN is declared dead; failback is the damped return to the primary once it is stable again.
Deliberate hysteresis in failback so a bouncing primary circuit does not make the gateway oscillate between WANs, dropping payment transactions and calls on every swing.

Carrier-engineered build-out (trenching, new drops, right-of-entry work) required to reach a site that is not yet served by existing facilities; it changes cost, timeline, and sometimes the whole technology decision.
A physical site visit by a technician; each avoidable one is the unit of waste that surveys, remote management, and accurate orders exist to prevent.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for site_qualification_and_service_activation work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Convert the deal as sold into a delivery scope: enumerate the sites, the services sold at each (primary internet, wireless backup, Wi-Fi, phones, cameras, payment connectivity), which carrier program each service rides under, and what the customer was actually promised about timing and behavior. Then state a per-service definition of activated - circuit live at the correct address, failover proven, bundled services cut over, evidence captured - so delivery closes against verifiable conditions instead of a feeling. Intake is also the moment anything sold-but-questionable (an assumed-serviceable address, an impossible date) is surfaced and challenged, because it is vastly cheaper to repair the promise now than on install week.

excluded: how the bundle was constructed or priced (sibling strategy KB)
compensation expectations (sibling lifecycle KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the deal scope, promised behavior, or site list is restated by the customer or the sales side

pros.claim: A per-service definition of activated prevents the installed-but-not-what-we-sold dispute
pros.example: the sale notes say backup exists so card payments never stop; intake records that failover must keep the payment terminal alive, which forces the test plan to include a live transaction

cons.claim: Heavy intake ceremony is waste on a one-site cable-plus-backup order
cons.example: a single taqueria with one circuit and one backup router needs a one-page scope, not a program-office intake packet

failure_modes: delivering to the order summary instead of what the customer was told in the sale
bundled services discovered at failover design time because intake never listed them
an assumed-serviceable address accepted into scope without being flagged for qualification
acceptance_tests: every site lists its sold services, the program each rides under, and a per-service activated condition with the evidence that will prove it
revisit_triggers: the customer adds or drops a service before install
qualification or the multi-site rollup contradicts a sold assumption

nodes.definition: Before any commitment at a site, verify the current rules of the carrier program the sale rides under: whether the sold product is still orderable in this market, which ordering portal or channel the agent must use and with what credentials, what the agent is authorized to say about install intervals, what representation and branding rules govern customer contact, and how the order must carry the agent-of-record identifiers. Partner programs revise product lists, footprints, and terms continuously - a product sheet from last quarter is a rumor, not an authority - so the check is against the live portal and current program bulletins, dated, every time.

excluded: comparing or selecting programs (sibling strategy KB)
compensation plan mechanics (sibling lifecycle KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the carrier revises program terms, the product list, or the ordering channel

pros.claim: Checking the live program before quoting an install prevents ordering a product the carrier quietly retired
pros.example: a fixed-wireless business plan pulled from new orders in this market while the agent's saved collateral still shows it

cons.claim: The check adds a delay at deal handoff and may need portal access only the program principal holds
cons.example: a sub-agent waiting on the master agency to confirm a product code before a same-day quote can go out

failure_modes: committing to a retired or footprint-restricted product from stale collateral
ordering through the wrong channel so the order is valid but unattributed to the agent
promising an install interval the current program no longer authorizes agents to quote
acceptance_tests: each commitment references a dated check of the live program source (portal, bulletin, or desk confirmation) for product, channel, and representation rules
revisit_triggers: a program bulletin, portal change, or product-list revision lands
an order is rejected or misattributed for a channel or tagging reason

nodes.definition: The conduct layer of the whole delivery: the agent sells and coordinates the carrier's service under a program and must say so plainly - never presenting as a carrier employee, never implying control over the carrier's network, dates, or billing. In qualification and activation this means coverage candor (a map is a claim to be verified on-site, not a promise), sober date language ('the carrier has committed this date and such dates move'), no fear-selling of outage catastrophe to push backup hardware a site does not need, and a comprehension check with less technical owners: before sign-off the owner can say in their own words what failover will and will not do. Trust built here is what the lifecycle side later lives on.

included: agent-status disclosure at every customer touch
excluded: sales-stage needs discovery ethics (sibling strategy KB)
ongoing escalation conduct after handoff (sibling lifecycle KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: program representation rules change or a misrepresentation complaint arises

pros.claim: Disclosure-first conduct removes the misrepresentation risk that can terminate an agent from a program
pros.example: an owner who knows the agent is the carrier's partner does not later claim they were deceived when a carrier bill or carrier tech shows up

cons.claim: Candor about date volatility and backup limits can soften urgency and slow a close at install-expectation time
cons.example: admitting the committed date can slip may push a customer to delay signing until the slower competitor confirms theirs

failure_modes: letting the customer believe the agent is the carrier and controls the outcome
selling backup on invented outage-cost terror instead of the site's real dependence on connectivity
a non-technical owner signing off on failover behavior they never actually understood
acceptance_tests: every written customer touch states the agent-of-carrier relationship, no communication asserts control over carrier dates or billing, and sign-off includes the owner restating failover behavior in their own words
revisit_triggers: the program's representation or branding rules change
a customer complaint or misunderstanding about who the agent is surfaces

nodes.definition: Establish what the carrier can actually deliver at the exact service address - street number, suite, unit, floor - using the carrier's qualification tools, and where the tool result is ambiguous, a human confirmation from the carrier's serviceability desk. Serviceability is a per-address fact and nothing else is evidence: not the building next door, not another suite in the same building (which may sit on a different wiring closet), not the marketing footprint map. Capture the qual as a record - date, the address string exactly as qualified, technology and tier returned, and any qual reference the carrier issues - because the order must be entered against that record and later disputes are adjudicated against it.

included: carrier qual tool and desk confirmation
excluded: wireless signal assessment (its own node)
choosing among the qualified options (technology matrix)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a qual re-run, order rejection, or footprint change contradicts the stored serviceability result

pros.claim: A dated suite-level qual record makes the later order defensible when the carrier's own systems disagree with themselves
pros.example: install is refused because the address is suddenly shown unserved; the qual reference from three weeks earlier forces an escalated re-check instead of a dead order

cons.claim: Qual tools are conservative and sometimes wrongly refuse a servable address, costing deals if taken as final
cons.example: a new-build suite the tool has never heard of quals as unserved until the desk manually validates the address

failure_modes: qualifying the building address while the customer's suite has no path from the wiring closet
quoting from the footprint map and discovering non-serviceability after contract
an undated, unreferenced qual that cannot support an order dispute
acceptance_tests: every site has a dated qual record at suite-level granularity with technology, tier, and the carrier's qual reference where issued, and no commitment cites a map or neighboring address as evidence
revisit_triggers: the carrier's footprint or qual result changes for a tracked address
an order rejection or install refusal contradicts the stored qual

nodes.definition: Decide whether 5G/LTE will actually work at this site - as backup, or as fixed-wireless primary - by measurement, not map. Coverage maps are optimistic claims; the decidable facts are on-site readings (RSRP, SINR, band) taken where the equipment would actually live: at the intended router location, at window and high-shelf alternatives, and at exterior mount candidates, during business hours when the cell is loaded. Building physics routinely turns a strong outdoor signal into an unusable indoor one - metal roofs, low-E glass, deep warehouse floors - so the assessment concludes with a placement-and-antenna decision (internal placement, window mount, or external antenna) and the readings that justify it, before any hardware is ordered.

included: on-site RSRP/SINR/band readings at candidate locations
excluded: wireline qualification (its own node)
the failover policy that uses the wireless path (failover design)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: new on-site readings, site physical changes, or carrier radio-network changes in the area

pros.claim: Measured indoor readings prevent shipping a backup that cannot hold a payment transaction when it is finally needed
pros.example: a restaurant whose map coverage is excellent but whose kitchen-adjacent equipment shelf reads unusable SINR until a window mount is added

cons.claim: A signal snapshot is one moment on one day; congestion and network changes can degrade a site that measured fine
cons.example: a site measured on a quiet morning that underperforms every Friday evening when the local cell saturates

failure_modes: trusting the coverage map and discovering dead indoor signal at failover test
measuring at the door instead of where the router will actually sit
skipping the loaded-hours reading and missing congestion-driven degradation
acceptance_tests: each site has recorded readings at the chosen location plus at least one alternative, taken during business hours, and the placement/antenna decision cites them
revisit_triggers: reported backup underperformance after activation
physical changes at the site (new racking, construction) or carrier network changes in the area

nodes.definition: Turn the qual and coverage facts into the feasible technology set for the site - fiber, cable, copper-class wireline, fixed wireless - and select the primary-plus-backup pairing with failure independence as the governing criterion: a backup that rides the same conduit, the same pole line, or the same operator network as the primary is theater, not resilience. Prefer pairings where the physical path and the failure domain differ, typically a wireline primary with a different network's wireless backup; where true diversity is not available, say so and record the shared-fate risk that remains rather than implying independence that does not exist. The matrix also captures what each option means for the services sold (speed class, static addressing availability, install interval class).

excluded: pricing and margin of the options (sibling strategy KB)
the gateway behavior that exploits the pairing (failover design)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: qual results, coverage readings, or orderable products at the address change

pros.claim: Choosing on failure independence makes the backup worth what the customer pays for it
pros.example: cable primary paired with a different operator's 5G backup keeps a pharmacy transacting through a neighborhood cable cut that takes out every same-network competitor on the street

cons.claim: The most diverse pairing is not always orderable or affordable at a given address
cons.example: a rural site where the only wireline is one carrier's copper and the strongest wireless is that same carrier's cell - diversity is partial and must be disclosed, not invented

failure_modes: pairing primary and backup on the same physical path or operator and calling it redundancy
selecting fixed-wireless primary where measured signal only supports backup duty
hiding residual shared-fate risk instead of recording it
acceptance_tests: each site's chosen pairing states the physical path and operator of both legs, the independence achieved, and any residual shared fate in writing
revisit_triggers: a new technology or carrier becomes orderable at the address
an outage reveals shared fate the matrix missed

nodes.definition: For a customer with several locations, roll the per-site qual and pairing results into one portfolio view: which sites the preferred carrier serves and on what technology, which need a different carrier or pairing, which are unserviceable on acceptable terms, and what all of that does to the uniformity the deal was sold on. The rollup exists to reset expectations before contracts: a three-store chain sold 'the same setup everywhere' must hear early that store two gets a different technology or a later date, and the reset flows back into the deal scope rather than surfacing as an install-week surprise. It also sequences the rollout - which site goes first as the template, and what learned there changes the rest.

excluded: multi-site account strategy and revenue planning (sibling strategy KB)
per-site delivery mechanics (other nodes)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: site list changes or a re-qual alters a site's feasible technology set

pros.claim: Surfacing divergent sites before contracts converts a delivery crisis into a scoped exception
pros.example: the flagship location quals only for a slower technology; the customer agrees to a different pairing there in writing instead of discovering it on opening week

cons.claim: Portfolio-level honesty can shrink or kill the deal when a key site is unserviceable
cons.example: the anchor store cannot be served on acceptable terms and the customer pauses the whole rollout

failure_modes: quoting the portfolio off one flagship site's qual
letting an unserviceable site ride silently in the contract until its install fails
sequencing the hardest site first and burning the customer's patience on the template
acceptance_tests: the rollup lists every site with its qual outcome, pairing, and any divergence from the sold uniform design, acknowledged by the customer before contracts
revisit_triggers: a site is added to or dropped from the rollout
a re-qual changes any site's feasible set

nodes.definition: Walk the site before ordering and record what install day will depend on: where the demarc/MPOE is and whether the customer's suite has usable inside wiring from it; where the gateway and wireless unit will live, with power, space, and ventilation confirmed; the cable paths and their obstacles (firewalls, ceilings, tenant boundaries); where the wireless readings were strongest and what mount that implies; and photographs of all of it. The survey converts design assumptions into observed facts and produces the artifact the install runs on. A skipped survey is not a saved hour - it is discovered later as a stalled carrier tech, a missing outlet, or an antenna with no permissible mount, each costing a truck roll and a date.

included: equipment location with power and space
mount and path findings with photos
excluded: consent and permit clearance (its own node)
the failover policy design (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: site physical changes or install-day findings that contradict the survey artifact

pros.claim: A photographed survey lets install day proceed without the agent physically present at every site
pros.example: the carrier tech calls from the site and the coordinator answers from the survey photos: the demarc is behind the stockroom door and the gateway shelf is above it

cons.claim: Surveys cost a visit per site and can be disproportionate for simple storefronts
cons.example: a small office suite two doors from the wiring closet where a phone-call walkthrough with the tenant would have sufficed

failure_modes: no one checked whether the suite has a path from the MPOE and the standard install cannot complete
the planned equipment corner has no power circuit
survey notes without photos that cannot answer install-day questions remotely
acceptance_tests: the survey artifact records demarc location, wiring path status, powered equipment location, mount decision, and photographs for each of them
revisit_triggers: the site is remodeled or the tenant moves suites before install
install-day findings contradict the survey

nodes.definition: Identify and clear what the building imposes before dates are committed: landlord or property-manager consent for drilling, conduit runs, roof or exterior antenna mounts; access rules for risers, shared telecom rooms, and after-hours work; and the class of local permissions exterior work can trigger - named here as an obligation class, with current rules verified against the local jurisdiction and the property's own lease terms, never asserted from memory. Consent is obtained in writing before the order commits install dates, because a roof denied after ordering strands the antenna design, and a property manager surprised by a drill is a relationship the customer, not the agent, has to live with.

included: permit obligation class with verify-current-rules flag
excluded: asserting specific permit requirements as fact
performing regulated electrical or structural work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: building management, lease terms, or local permitting rules change

pros.claim: Written consent before ordering prevents the stalled-install pattern where the carrier tech arrives and the building says no
pros.example: a strip-mall landlord's emailed approval for one exterior antenna mount attached to the order file before the FOC is accepted

cons.claim: Chasing consent adds days or weeks of latency the customer perceives as agent slowness
cons.example: an out-of-state property-management company that takes three weeks to answer a one-paragraph mount request

failure_modes: drilling or mounting first and asking permission after
assuming the tenant can authorize roof work the lease reserves to the landlord
treating permit requirements as known instead of verifying the current local rules
acceptance_tests: any exterior or structural work item carries written consent from the authorized party and a note of the permit class verified with the local jurisdiction before install dates are committed
revisit_triggers: building ownership or management changes
the mount or path design changes after consent was given

nodes.definition: Design, in writing, how the site behaves when the primary fails: which gateway arbitrates the two WANs; what health checks declare the primary dead (and against which probe targets, so one flaky DNS server does not trigger a site-wide swing); which services fail over and which are deliberately shed on the bandwidth-limited wireless path; how statically-bound and NAT-sensitive services behave when the WAN address changes; and how the site returns to primary - damped failback so a flapping circuit cannot oscillate the gateway. The design is written against the bundled-service map: the payment path and phones typically must survive, camera cloud upload is often shed, and every survive/shed choice is a recorded decision the customer has seen, not an accident of default config.

excluded: the physical pairing choice (technology matrix)
device-level configuration steps (implementation node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: bundled-service changes, test failures, or real-outage behavior that contradicts the design

pros.claim: A written survive/shed policy converts limited backup bandwidth into predictable business continuity
pros.example: the design states card payments and phones ride the backup while cameras pause uploads; the owner has agreed to exactly that trade before an outage makes it visible

cons.claim: Design effort exceeds the need at tiny sites with one critical device
cons.example: a kiosk with a single payment terminal needs a one-line policy, not a service-by-service failover matrix

failure_modes: failing everything over onto a wireless path that cannot carry it, so the backup collapses under its own load
statically-bound services silently breaking on WAN address change because nobody designed for it
no failback damping, so a bouncing primary drops every call and transaction twice per bounce
acceptance_tests: the design document names the health checks and probe targets, the per-service survive/shed policy acknowledged by the customer, and the failback damping behavior
revisit_triggers: a bundled service is added or its criticality changes
the failover test or a real outage contradicts the designed behavior

nodes.definition: Inventory everything that will ride the circuit at this site - Wi-Fi, phones, POS and payment terminals, cameras, music, back-office SaaS - and record what each needs from the network: bandwidth class, static addressing or pinned-port dependencies, tolerance of a WAN change, and criticality to the business's ability to trade. The map is the input both failover design and cutover sequencing run on, and it is where anything life-safety adjacent - alarm panels, elevator phones, fire lines - is identified, flagged, and referred to the licensed responsible vendor rather than migrated by the agent. A service that is not on the map will be discovered at the worst possible moment: mid-outage or mid-cutover.

excluded: installing or configuring the bundled services themselves
designing life-safety communication paths

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new riding service appears or an outage exposes an unmapped dependency

pros.claim: A complete map is what makes the failover policy a business decision instead of a router default
pros.example: discovering the card terminal is pinned to a static route through the old modem before failover design, not during the first outage

cons.claim: The map is only as good as what the customer remembers to mention
cons.example: an owner who forgets the walk-in freezer's temperature monitor dials out over the internet until it fails silently after cutover

failure_modes: an unmapped alarm panel migrated off its monitored line by accident
criticality guessed by the agent instead of stated by the owner
the map built from the quote instead of a walk of what is actually plugged in
acceptance_tests: the map lists every discovered riding service with bandwidth class, addressing dependency, WAN-change tolerance, and owner-stated criticality, and any life-safety item carries a licensed-vendor referral note
revisit_triggers: a new bundled service is sold or discovered at the site
cutover or an outage reveals an unmapped dependency

nodes.definition: Enter the carrier order so it is right the first time: the service address exactly as the qual record qualified it (suite included), the product and tier the qual returned, the correct contract term and equipment, the install type, and the program's agent-of-record identifiers so the activation is attributed under the program's mechanism - attribution errors are repaired through the carrier's correction process slowly, if at all, and tracking the resulting compensation belongs to the lifecycle KB; this node's whole job is a clean, attributable order. A wrong order is not casually edited: many carrier systems can only cancel-and-rebook, which surrenders the queue position and the install date the customer has already planned around.

included: order entry against the qual record
excluded: compensation amounts and tracking (sibling lifecycle KB)
chasing the order after submission (provisioning node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: order rejections, misattributed activations, or changes to the program's ordering requirements

pros.claim: Entering the order verbatim from the qual record removes the largest single source of install delay the agent controls
pros.example: the address entered as qualified, down to 'Ste B', so the order does not fall out for manual address review

cons.claim: Careful order assembly is slower than firing the portal form from memory, and the discipline feels bureaucratic on routine orders
cons.example: a same-technology second site where copying the first site's order would be faster - and would carry the first site's suite number into the second site's order

failure_modes: the order address diverging from the qualified address and falling out or installing at the wrong suite
a missing or wrong agent code so the activation exists but is not attributed to the agent
editing a live order into a cancel-and-rebook that loses the committed date
acceptance_tests: each submitted order matches its qual record on address, product, and tier, carries the current program's agent-of-record identifiers, and any post-submission change is assessed for cancel-and-rebook risk before it is requested
revisit_triggers: an order falls out, is rejected, or activates unattributed
the program changes its ordering channel or identifier scheme

nodes.definition: Own the order between submission and install: track status through the portal or partner desk, catch jeopardy codes and fallout early, hold the FOC date against the customer's calendar, schedule the install appointment with a person who can actually grant access, and communicate date movement to the customer as it happens - not after the carrier's own notice beats the agent to it. The agent cannot make the carrier faster; the discipline is removing the failure modes the agent does control: unreachable site contacts, locked doors, missed appointment windows, and the customer learning about a slip from anyone but the agent. Every date given to the customer is the carrier's committed date, named as such, never an agent invention.

excluded: special-construction handling (its own node)
install-day on-site management (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: order status events, FOC changes, or site-contact changes on open orders

pros.claim: Being first with bad news is the cheapest trust purchase in the whole delivery
pros.example: calling the owner about a two-week slip the hour the jeopardy code posts, with the replan already drafted, instead of letting the carrier's automated text land first

cons.claim: Daily order-chasing across many carriers is unbillable coordination time that scales linearly with open orders
cons.example: an agent with a dozen open installs spending each morning walking portals that have not changed since yesterday

failure_modes: an order sitting in fallout for a week because nobody was watching
an install appointment missed because the listed site contact was on vacation
the customer hearing a date change from the carrier before the agent
acceptance_tests: every open order has a current status checked on a stated cadence, a reachable access-granting site contact, and a log showing the customer was told of each date change when it posted
revisit_triggers: a jeopardy code, fallout, or FOC change posts
the site contact or access situation changes

nodes.definition: Manage install day so the carrier tech's visit produces a working circuit where the design needs it: someone with keys and authority present for the whole window, the survey artifact in hand or on the phone, the intended equipment location and any inside-wiring question resolved or escalated while the tech is still on site, and the demarcation clarified - what the carrier tech owns versus what the agent or the customer's contractor completes past the demarc. Before the tech leaves, the circuit is confirmed live and the handoff point (jack, ONT, modem) sits where the failover gateway can actually reach it, because re-summoning a carrier tech to move a termination is a multi-week penalty for a five-minute conversation not had.

included: demarc handoff verification before the tech leaves
excluded: gateway and failover configuration (its own node)
performing regulated inside-wiring work

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: install outcomes that deviate from the survey or reschedule

pros.claim: Catching a termination-point problem while the tech is on site converts a multi-week re-dispatch into a same-visit fix
pros.example: the tech plans to terminate at the MPOE; the coordinator, reached by phone, redirects to the stockroom jack per the survey before the tech closes the ticket

cons.claim: Covering every install window personally does not scale past a handful of concurrent sites
cons.example: two installs booked the same morning in different towns forcing the agent to phone-cover one blind

failure_modes: the tech arrives to a locked site and the order reschedules weeks out
the circuit terminated at a point the gateway cannot reach
the tech leaves before anyone confirms the circuit is actually live
acceptance_tests: each install has a confirmed access-granting person for the window, and the closing check confirms circuit live at a termination point matching the survey before the tech departs
revisit_triggers: an install reschedules or fails
the termination point deviates from the survey

nodes.definition: Handle the orders that stop being routine: special construction the carrier must engineer and often prices separately, right-of-entry negotiations with the property, and FOC dates that slip repeatedly. The play is expectation surgery plus interim service: tell the customer the truth about the slip and its mechanism (what special construction is, who is waiting on whom), and where the business must open before wireline arrives, activate the wireless unit as a temporary primary - the same hardware that later becomes the backup - with its limits stated plainly rather than sold as equivalent. Long delays are also the decision point for re-quoting a different technology from the matrix instead of riding a build-out that keeps moving.

excluded: negotiating construction charges as if the agent controlled them
the interim unit's configuration details (implementation node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: construction status, FOC movement, or interim-period thresholds being crossed

pros.claim: Wireless-first interim activation lets the customer open on schedule while the build-out runs
pros.example: a new restaurant opens on its announced date on the 5G unit with the payment path prioritized, and the fiber lands three weeks later as designed

cons.claim: An interim wireless primary can quietly become permanent, leaving the site without true redundancy
cons.example: the build-out stalls indefinitely and nobody converts the deal, so the site runs one wireless path with no backup for months

failure_modes: holding the original promised date in customer communications while the FOC slips
selling the interim wireless as equivalent to the ordered wireline
no decision trigger for abandoning a chronically slipping build-out
acceptance_tests: every slipped order shows a customer communication with the real mechanism and new date, and any interim wireless activation carries a written statement of its limits and a planned conversion
revisit_triggers: a further FOC slip or construction quote change posts
the interim period exceeds the threshold the customer agreed to

nodes.definition: Implement the written design on the gateway: WAN priority and health checks against multiple probe targets so one dead DNS server cannot trigger a site-wide swing; failback hysteresis per the design; per-service policy for what uses the wireless path and what is shed; alerting that tells the agent when the site is running on backup and when backup usage approaches any plan threshold the wireless line carries; and remote management access so the site can be seen and fixed without a truck roll. Configuration is complete when it matches the design document line by line - not when the internet happens to work - and the delta between design and device is zero or documented.

excluded: the design decisions themselves (design node)
bundled-service device configuration

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: design revisions or operational discoveries of drift and alert gaps

pros.claim: On-backup alerting turns silent degradation into a service event the agent handles before the customer notices
pros.example: the gateway alerts that the site failed over at 6 a.m.; the agent has the carrier ticket open before the owner arrives to a store that kept trading

cons.claim: Remote management access is an attack surface and a responsibility, not a freebie
cons.example: a fleet of gateways reachable with one shared credential is one leak away from every site being someone else's gateway

failure_modes: health checks probing a single target that fails independently of the WAN
config drifting from the design with no record of why
no alert on backup usage so a capped wireless line dies silently mid-outage
acceptance_tests: the device configuration is diffed against the design document with zero undocumented deltas, alerting fires on failover and on usage thresholds, and remote access uses per-site credentials
revisit_triggers: the design changes
an alert gap or config drift is discovered in operation

nodes.definition: Prove the design before the customer relies on it: in an agreed low-impact window, physically fail the primary - pull the WAN cable, do not merely simulate - observe the gateway detect and switch, and verify that the services that must survive actually do: run a live card transaction, make and receive a phone call, confirm what the staff will see and for how long. Measure the switchover gap, then restore the primary and confirm damped failback with no oscillation. Record all of it - date, participants, results, gaps - because this record is what the handoff stands on and what any future 'it did not fail over' dispute is settled against. An untested failover is a story the site tells itself, not a service anyone bought.

included: physical pulled-primary test in an agreed window
excluded: fixing what the test finds (back to design/config)
carrier-side network testing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: design or equipment changes, or real-outage behavior diverging from the test record

pros.claim: A live-transaction test is the only honest proof the survive policy survives
pros.example: the pulled-plug test reveals the card terminal re-registers for four minutes on WAN change - found in a Tuesday-morning window, not during a Saturday rush outage

cons.claim: A real test briefly disrupts a live business and needs the owner's buy-in to schedule
cons.example: a store that cannot accept even a planned two-minute payment pause until after hours, pushing the test to an evening window

failure_modes: declaring failover done from a dashboard simulation that never dropped the physical link
testing connectivity but never exercising the payment or voice path
skipping the failback half so the first real recovery becomes the flap test
acceptance_tests: a dated test record exists showing a physical primary failure, the exercised critical services with outcomes, the observed switchover gap, and a clean damped failback
revisit_triggers: any change to the design, the gateway, or the critical-service set
a real outage behaves differently than the recorded test

nodes.definition: Before sign-off, verify the activated service against the order and the sale: speed-test at the demarc against the ordered tier's expected band (a band, because delivered throughput varies - the check is gross mismatch, not decimal points), confirm static addressing and any port or DNS specifics arrived as ordered, check that the carrier account shows the product, term, and plan that were sold, and confirm when billing starts relative to activation under the program's terms. Mismatches get corrected while the install is still an open order and the carrier's install machinery is still engaged; after sign-off the same mismatch becomes a billing dispute and a re-provisioning ticket measured in weeks.

included: delivered-versus-ordered checks on speed band, addressing, plan, and term
correction while the order is open
excluded: failover behavior proof (test protocol)
ongoing billing-dispute handling after handoff (sibling lifecycle KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: post-sign-off mismatches or mid-order plan changes by the carrier

pros.claim: Catching a wrong provisioned tier before sign-off converts weeks of dispute into a same-day correction
pros.example: the demarc speed test lands far below the ordered tier's band; the installing tech's own ticket gets the profile fixed before anyone leaves

cons.claim: Over-literal verification can block sign-off on differences that do not matter to the business
cons.example: holding a restaurant's handoff over a modest speed-test shortfall well within normal variance for the technology

failure_modes: signing off without a demarc-level speed test and inheriting a wrong profile as a billing dispute
static addresses ordered but never delivered, discovered when the bundled installer needs them
billing started before activation and nobody checked the program's terms for which is correct
acceptance_tests: a verification record shows the demarc speed test against the ordered band, delivered addressing, the carrier-account plan and term matching the order, and the billing-start check
revisit_triggers: a mismatch is found post-sign-off
the carrier changes the plan or tier definitions mid-order

nodes.definition: Hand the customer a package they can operate from: what was installed and where (with the survey photos), how failover behaves in their terms - what keeps working, what pauses, what staff will notice and for roughly how long - who to call for what (the carrier for network faults on its side of the demarc, the agent for the failover gear and for coordination), equipment ownership and return obligations, and admin credentials stored and transferred responsibly. On money, the package points at the carrier's own order confirmation as the authority on price and term rather than restating figures the agent does not control. It is written for the least technical person who will be alone with a dead connection at eight on a Saturday morning.

excluded: restating carrier pricing as agent-authored fact
ongoing support operations (sibling lifecycle KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: site changes or support incidents revealing documentation gaps

pros.claim: A who-to-call split that matches the demarc stops the customer from burning days in the wrong queue
pros.example: the laminated one-pager by the router says outage-light pattern A means call the carrier with the account number printed below, pattern B means call the agent

cons.claim: Documentation nobody reads is cost without effect if it is not physically and verbally delivered
cons.example: a beautiful PDF in an inbox while the store manager who actually opens the site never hears the two-minute failover explanation

failure_modes: handoff that restates prices from memory instead of pointing at the carrier's order confirmation
admin credentials left at defaults or held only in the agent's head
failover behavior described in network jargon the owner cannot act on
acceptance_tests: the package contains the as-installed record, the plain-language failover description, the demarc-aligned contact split, credential handling, and a pointer to the carrier's order confirmation for all figures
revisit_triggers: equipment, services, or contacts at the site change
a support incident shows the package failed its reader

nodes.definition: Cut the bundled services over to the new circuit in an order that never strands the business's ability to trade: verify the new circuit first, move the least critical service as the canary, keep the payment path and phones on their existing connectivity until the new path has demonstrably carried them, and only then release the old service - the old circuit is the rollback plan and is not disconnected until the new one has earned its keep. Each bundled installer (Wi-Fi, VoIP, cameras, POS) receives the site facts their install needs - addressing plan, which port or VLAN is theirs, how failover behaves - so their work lands inside the failover design instead of quietly undoing it.

included: staged cutover with canary and rollback
site-fact handoff to each bundled installer
excluded: performing the bundled services' own installs
life-safety path migration (licensed referral only)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: mid-cutover service additions or step failures

pros.claim: Keeping the old circuit as rollback makes every cutover step reversible until the new path is proven
pros.example: the POS moves last and the old cable modem stays live for the overlap week, so a bad first day is a plug swap instead of an outage

cons.claim: Overlap means paying for two services for a period, which the customer must accept knowingly
cons.example: an owner surprised by one overlapping bill cancels the old service early and removes the rollback the sequence depended on

failure_modes: cutting every service at once and turning one bad cable into a whole-business outage
a bundled installer bypassing the failover gateway and putting the POS on the raw modem
the old service disconnected before the new path ever carried the payment traffic
acceptance_tests: the cutover plan shows the staged order with the trading-critical services last, the old-service release condition, and a per-installer site-fact sheet for every bundled service
revisit_triggers: a bundled service is added mid-cutover
a canary step fails or an installer deviates from the site facts

nodes.definition: Close delivery by assembling the record the account's future stands on: the qual evidence, the survey artifact, order confirmations, the activation date per service, the verification results, the failover test record, and the customer's handoff acknowledgment - packaged per site and per service. This record is what the lifecycle layer consumes for compensation tracking, renewal timing, and dispute defense (the tracking itself is that KB's territory; producing the defensible record is this one's), and it is delivery's final gate: a site whose internet works but whose record is incomplete is not done, because six months from now the record is the only part of the install anyone can still see.

excluded: compensation calculation and tracking (sibling lifecycle KB)
renewal and churn management (sibling lifecycle KB)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: downstream consumers report evidence gaps or a dispute exposes a missing item

pros.claim: A complete activation record is the raw material of every future compensation or service dispute the agent will win
pros.example: months later the activation is questioned; the record's order confirmation, activation date, and signed acknowledgment settle it in one email

cons.claim: Record assembly is unglamorous closing work that pressure pushes to 'later', which means never
cons.example: three installs closing the same week and the evidence folders started after memories have already blurred which site tested when

failure_modes: delivery declared done on a working circuit with no assembled evidence
records scattered across inboxes and portals rather than packaged per site
the handoff acknowledgment never collected, leaving sign-off deniable
acceptance_tests: each closed site has a single package containing qual, survey, order confirmations, activation dates, verification and failover-test records, and the customer acknowledgment
revisit_triggers: the lifecycle layer reports a missing or insufficient evidence item
a dispute exercises the record and finds a gap

edges.why_related: the programs named in the delivery scope are the ones whose current rules must be verified
the site list and sold services from intake define which addresses get qualified for what
the sold bundle at intake seeds the inventory of services that will ride the circuit
whether wireless is sold as backup or primary at each site comes from the intake scope and shapes the assessment
the order's channel, product codes, and agent-of-record identifiers come from the current program rules
the program's representation and branding rules define what the disclosure conduct must satisfy
the matrix's feasible wireline options are exactly what the qual returned for the address
measured signal decides whether fixed wireless enters the matrix as backup-capable or primary-capable
the backup path's measured capacity bounds what the survive/shed policy can promise
the chosen pairing determines what the survey must verify (demarc reach, mount points, antenna candidates)
the order encodes the pairing's selected product and tier for the site
the rollup aggregates the per-address qual results across the customer's sites
the survey's mount and path findings define which consents and permit classes must be cleared
the design places the gateway and antenna where the survey found power, space, and signal
the survive/shed policy is written service by service against the dependency map
configuration implements the written design and is checked against it line by line
the map's critical services are the ones the test must exercise live
the test proves the implemented configuration, not the design intent
verification runs at the demarc the install day delivered and confirmed live
the order record is the baseline the delivered service is verified against
the handoff documents a service already verified against the order, never an unverified one
the package's failover description restates what the test actually demonstrated
cutover of trading-critical services waits for the proven failover path
bundled installers receive delivered addressing and plan facts only after they are verified
the customer's acknowledged handoff is a required item in the closing record
completed cutovers per bundled service are evidence the closing record must contain
handoff language must keep the agent/carrier split honest and defer to carrier documents on figures
every date given to the customer must be named as the carrier's committed date, never an agent invention
no drilling, mounting, or riser work proceeds on install day without the written consents in hand
pipeline coordination begins the moment a clean order is submitted and owns it to install day
the coordinated appointment and access readiness hand directly into managing the install visit
where wireline options are weak the matrix wants fixed wireless as primary, while the measured indoor signal may only support backup duty
edges.resolution_rule: measured on-site readings govern: below the design threshold fixed wireless is not offered as primary regardless of footprint claims, and the limitation is disclosed rather than worked around

edges.why_related: holding the customer's original promised date fights the reality of a slipping FOC and construction timeline
edges.resolution_rule: reality wins immediately: dates are reset on carrier evidence the day it posts, with the slip mechanism explained, and a fixed opening is bridged with interim wireless rather than a silently held promise

edges.why_related: closing the install same-day pressures against running a deliberately disruptive pulled-plug test on a live business
edges.resolution_rule: the test is never skipped: if same-day disruption is unacceptable, a dated test window is scheduled and handoff is not declared complete until the test record exists

edges.why_related: the ambition to fail everything over collides with the mapped reality of limited backup capacity and per-service demands
edges.resolution_rule: the map's owner-stated criticality ranking governs: trading-critical services survive, bulk consumers are shed, and a full-failover promise requires measured backup capacity to back it

edges.why_related: the mount and placement chosen from survey readings causally determine the backup performance the test observes
verification evidence is what makes the closing record defensible in later disputes
a failed or surprising test sends the design back for revision before any handoff
unserviceable or divergent sites in the rollup force the delivery scope and its promises to be restated
both are per-site fact-finding disciplines that replace assumption with evidence - one against carrier records, one against measured radio signal

conflict_axes.name: coverage_map_optimism_vs_measured_signal
conflict_axes.description: Carrier coverage maps and footprint claims invite commitments that on-site indoor measurement may not support.
poles: trust the coverage map and move fast
commit only on measured on-site signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: maps select candidate sites; only business-hours indoor readings at the equipment location authorize an order or a primary-duty claim

conflict_axes.name: order_speed_vs_order_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: Submitting the order fast feels like progress, but an error triggers cancel-and-rebook that loses more time than the care would have cost.
poles: submit immediately
verify every field against the qual record first
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: accuracy wins: a clean order beats an early wrong one because rebooking surrenders the queue position and the committed date

conflict_axes.name: promised_date_vs_carrier_reality
conflict_axes.description: The customer plans around a date, while FOC dates and construction timelines move for reasons the agent does not control.
poles: protect the promised date in communications
reset dates on carrier evidence as it posts
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: communicate the carrier's committed date as such, reset it the day evidence changes, and bridge fixed openings with interim wireless

conflict_axes.name: path_diversity_vs_pairing_convenience
conflict_axes.description: The easiest backup to order often shares a pole line, conduit, or operator network with the primary, which guts its value in a real outage.
poles: order the convenient same-infrastructure backup
insist on independent physical path and failure domain
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: diversity governs the pairing choice; where full independence is unavailable the residual shared fate is disclosed in writing, never implied away

conflict_axes.name: full_failover_ambition_vs_backup_capacity
conflict_axes.description: Failing every service over sounds like the premium outcome but can collapse a bandwidth-limited wireless path exactly when it matters.
poles: fail everything over
prioritize trading-critical services and shed the rest
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the survive/shed policy follows the owner-stated criticality ranking and the measured backup capacity, and the customer sees the trade before an outage does

conflict_axes.name: test_disruption_vs_handoff_confidence
conflict_axes.description: A physical pulled-plug test briefly disrupts a live business, and skipping it closes the install faster at the price of an unproven backup.
poles: skip or simulate the test to avoid disruption
physically test before any reliance
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: schedule an agreed low-impact window and test for real; handoff is not declared while the failover claim rests on simulation

conflict_axes.name: agent_ownership_vs_carrier_control
conflict_axes.description: The agent owns the customer experience of delivery while the carrier controls provisioning, dates, and the install workforce.
poles: push the carrier on everything as if in control
wait passively on carrier machinery
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: own what the agent controls (accuracy, access, communication, escalation timing) and represent the rest honestly as the carrier's committed process

conflict_axes.name: cutover_speed_vs_service_continuity
conflict_axes.description: Moving all bundled services to the new circuit at once finishes the job quickly but turns any surprise into a whole-business outage.
poles: cut everything over at once
stage the cutover with canary and rollback
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stage with the least critical service first and the payment path last, keeping the old service live as rollback until the new path has carried the critical traffic

conflict_axes.name: disclosure_candor_vs_deal_momentum
conflict_axes.description: Honest talk about agent status, date volatility, and backup limits can slow a close that fear or vagueness would speed up.
poles: soften the caveats to keep momentum
disclose fully even when it slows the close
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure wins every time: a deal closed on candor survives its first slip and its first outage, and program rules make misrepresentation an existential risk

conflict_axes.name: building_constraint_respect_vs_install_completion
conflict_axes.description: Finishing the install today may require drilling or mounting the landlord and local rules have not yet authorized.
poles: complete the work and regularize later
wait for written consent and verified permit class
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: consent and verification precede work: an unauthorized mount risks the customer's lease and the agent's standing, and the schedule absorbs the wait

edge_cases.description: The building address quals serviceable but the customer's suite has no wiring path from the closet the qual assumed
edge_cases.trigger: qualification run at building granularity for a multi-tenant property
edge_cases.mitigation: qual at suite granularity, confirm the inside-wiring path during the survey, and treat building-level quals as provisional until the suite path is seen

edge_cases.description: The coverage map shows strong 5G but the metal-roofed warehouse interior reads unusable at the equipment shelf
edge_cases.trigger: building materials attenuate an outdoor-strong signal indoors
edge_cases.mitigation: measure at the true equipment location, escalate to window or external antenna mounts with landlord consent, and refuse backup-duty claims the readings cannot support

edge_cases.description: Special construction pushes the wireline FOC past the customer's fixed opening day
edge_cases.trigger: a build-out requirement surfaces after ordering while the opening date cannot move
edge_cases.mitigation: activate the wireless unit as a stated-limits interim primary so the business opens, keep the wireline order moving, and convert to the designed pairing when it lands

edge_cases.description: Failover switches the WAN but the statically-bound card terminal drops and stays down until manually re-registered
edge_cases.trigger: a WAN address change breaks a service pinned to the primary's addressing
edge_cases.mitigation: map addressing dependencies before design, engineer the payment path to tolerate WAN change, and exercise a live transaction during the failover test

edge_cases.description: A multi-day primary outage silently exhausts the wireless line's usage threshold and the backup throttles mid-outage
edge_cases.trigger: extended failover consumes the backup plan's data allowance
edge_cases.mitigation: alert on backup usage thresholds, shed bulk consumers by policy, and treat a long outage as an active service event the agent manages rather than background failover

edge_cases.description: The order activates cleanly but carries a wrong or missing agent code, so the activation exists unattributed
edge_cases.trigger: attribution identifiers omitted or mistyped at order entry
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the current program's identifier scheme on every order before submission and file the carrier's correction process immediately on discovery, with the order record as evidence

edge_cases.description: The landlord denies roof access after the order with an external-antenna design is already placed
edge_cases.trigger: consent assumed rather than obtained before ordering
edge_cases.mitigation: obtain written consent before orders commit dates; on denial, redesign to window or interior placement from the survey's alternative readings before the install date burns

edge_cases.description: The carrier tech terminates at the MPOE and the suite needs an inside-wiring extension nobody scoped or priced
edge_cases.trigger: demarc-to-suite path never confirmed before install day
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm the demarc-to-suite path at survey, clarify in advance who performs and pays for extension work, and escalate while the tech is still on site

edge_cases.description: A bouncing primary circuit makes the gateway oscillate between WANs, dropping card transactions on every swing
edge_cases.trigger: failback configured without damping on an unstable primary
edge_cases.mitigation: require hold-down hysteresis before failback, verify damped behavior in the test's restore phase, and open a carrier ticket on the flapping primary as the root cause

edge_cases.description: The bundled-service walk finds the alarm panel and elevator phone riding the circuit being replaced
edge_cases.trigger: life-safety communication paths discovered on the connectivity being migrated
edge_cases.mitigation: flag and freeze those paths, refer them to the licensed alarm or elevator vendor, and sequence the cutover so nothing life-safety moves under the agent's hand

edge_cases.description: The demarc speed test lands far below the ordered tier's expected band at verification
edge_cases.trigger: a wrong provisioning profile applied on activation
edge_cases.mitigation: hold sign-off, drive the correction through the still-open install ticket, and re-test at the demarc before the customer accepts the service

edge_cases.description: The multi-site rollup shows the customer's flagship location unserviceable by the carrier the whole deal was sold on
edge_cases.trigger: portfolio qualification contradicts the sold uniform design
edge_cases.mitigation: surface the divergence before contracts, replan that site on a different pairing or carrier with the customer's written acknowledgment, and resequence the rollout around the exception

workflow.action: Intake the sold deal and define activated per service
workflow.description: Enumerate sites, services, programs, and promises; state the evidence that will close each service
workflow.artifact: delivery scope with per-service definition of activated
workflow.gate: every site lists sold services, program, and a verifiable activated condition

workflow.description: Check the live portal and bulletins for product availability, channel, representation rules, and identifiers
workflow.gate: no commitment precedes a dated check of the live program source

workflow.description: Run suite-level quals through the carrier's tools with desk confirmation where ambiguous
workflow.artifact: dated qual record per site with technology, tier, and reference
workflow.gate: each site has a suite-level qual record; no maps or neighbors cited as evidence

workflow.description: Take business-hours RSRP/SINR readings at candidate equipment locations and decide placement and antenna
workflow.artifact: signal readings with a placement-and-antenna decision
workflow.gate: the decision cites readings at the chosen location plus an alternative

workflow.action: Select the technology pairing per site
workflow.description: Build the feasible set from qual facts and choose primary plus backup on failure independence
workflow.artifact: pairing decision with independence rationale and residual shared fate
workflow.gate: both legs' physical path and operator are stated with any shared fate disclosed

workflow.description: Aggregate per-site outcomes, surface divergences and unserviceable sites, sequence the rollout
workflow.artifact: portfolio qual view acknowledged by the customer
workflow.gate: every divergence from the sold design is acknowledged before contracts

workflow.action: Survey the site and clear building constraints
workflow.description: Record demarc, wiring path, powered equipment location, mounts, and photos; obtain written consents and verify permit class
workflow.gate: install dates are not committed until the survey exists and consents are in hand

workflow.action: Map bundled services and design failover
workflow.description: Inventory riding services with requirements and criticality, then write the survive/shed, health-check, and failback design
workflow.artifact: dependency map and failover design document
workflow.gate: the survive/shed policy is written per service and acknowledged by the customer

workflow.description: Enter the order verbatim from the qual record with term, equipment, install type, and agent-of-record identifiers
workflow.artifact: submitted order matching the qual record
workflow.gate: order fields match the qual record and carry the current program's identifiers

workflow.action: Drive provisioning to a completed install
workflow.description: Track status and jeopardy, hold access readiness, manage install day and the demarc handoff, absorb construction delays honestly
workflow.artifact: order log with dated customer communications and install-day closure note
workflow.gate: circuit confirmed live at a termination point matching the survey before the tech departs

workflow.description: Implement the design on the gateway, then pull the primary in an agreed window and exercise payment and voice through switchover and damped failback
workflow.artifact: config-versus-design diff and dated failover test record
workflow.gate: zero undocumented config deltas and a test record with critical services exercised

workflow.action: Verify activation, hand off, and close the record
workflow.description: Verify delivered service against the order, deliver the customer package, stage bundled cutovers, and assemble the per-site evidence record
workflow.artifact: verification record, handoff package, cutover plan, and closing evidence package
workflow.gate: the closing package contains qual, survey, orders, verification, test record, and customer acknowledgment

priority_rationale: The frame nodes (deal intake, program verification, conduct) come first because every downstream commitment depends on knowing what was sold, what the current program actually permits, and how the agent may represent itself; qualification nodes convert addresses into facts that the matrix, survey, and design consume; ordering and provisioning run only on qualified, surveyed, consented sites; failover configuration and physical testing prove the design before anyone relies on it; and verification, handoff, and the closing evidence record come last because they compose everything prior into an activated, documented site the lifecycle layer can defend.

dominance_rules.rule: Measured per-address fact dominates any map, footprint, or assumption
dominance_rules.rationale: serviceability and signal are address-specific facts; everything else is marketing or hope
dominance_rules.trigger: a commitment is about to rest on a coverage map, a neighboring address, or a remembered footprint
dominance_rules.action: block the commitment until the qual record or on-site readings exist for that exact address

dominance_rules.rule: The current program's verified rules dominate remembered or archived program knowledge
dominance_rules.rationale: partner programs change product lists, channels, and terms continuously and without ceremony
dominance_rules.trigger: any commitment, order, or representation is about to rely on program knowledge without a dated check
dominance_rules.action: verify against the live portal, bulletin, or desk and date the check before proceeding

dominance_rules.rule: Honest affiliation disclosure dominates deal momentum
dominance_rules.rationale: misrepresenting carrier affiliation violates program rules and can end the agency itself
dominance_rules.trigger: softening or omitting the agent-of-carrier relationship would smooth a close or a difficult conversation
dominance_rules.action: state the relationship plainly and let the deal carry its true shape

dominance_rules.rationale: a backup sharing the primary's path or operator fails with it, making the customer's payment worthless
dominance_rules.trigger: the easy-to-order backup shares infrastructure with the primary
dominance_rules.action: select the diverse pairing where orderable, and where it is not, disclose the residual shared fate in writing

dominance_rules.rationale: many carrier systems repair errors only by cancel-and-rebook, which loses the queue position and the date
dominance_rules.trigger: pressure to submit before fields are verified against the qual record
dominance_rules.action: verify address, product, tier, term, and identifiers against the qual record first, then submit

dominance_rules.rule: The physical failover test dominates install-closure pressure
dominance_rules.rationale: an untested failover is an unverified claim the customer is already paying for
dominance_rules.trigger: a site is about to be handed off with failover simulated, assumed, or untested
dominance_rules.action: hold handoff and schedule the pulled-primary test window; no test record, no completion

dominance_rules.rule: Written consent and verified permit class dominate install completion
dominance_rules.rationale: unauthorized drilling or mounting endangers the customer's lease and the agent's standing beyond the install
dominance_rules.trigger: finishing today's work requires building modifications not yet authorized
dominance_rules.action: stop the physical work, obtain the consent or verification, and reschedule the affected step

dominance_rules.rule: Licensed referral dominates bundle completeness on life-safety paths
dominance_rules.rationale: alarm, elevator, and fire communication paths carry regulatory and life-safety weight the agent must not touch
dominance_rules.trigger: a life-safety service is found riding connectivity the agent is migrating
dominance_rules.action: freeze that path, refer it to the licensed responsible vendor, and sequence around it

dominance_rules.rule: Verification against the order dominates sign-off eagerness
dominance_rules.rationale: a mismatch corrected inside the open order is same-day work; after sign-off it is weeks of dispute
dominance_rules.trigger: sign-off is proposed before delivered speed band, addressing, plan, and billing start are checked
dominance_rules.action: run the verification record first and route any mismatch through the still-open order

dominance_rules.rationale: the business's ability to trade is the thing the whole install exists to protect
dominance_rules.trigger: a plan proposes moving trading-critical services before the new path has carried them
dominance_rules.action: re-stage with a canary first, critical services last, and the old service held as rollback until proven

anti_rework_rules.rule: Qualify the exact suite-level address before quoting or ordering anything
anti_rework_rules.prevents: cancel-and-rebook cycles and wrong-suite installs from building-level or assumed serviceability

anti_rework_rules.rule: Take on-site signal readings before ordering wireless hardware or promising backup behavior
anti_rework_rules.prevents: returned equipment and a redesign after the installed unit cannot hold a transaction indoors

anti_rework_rules.rule: Survey demarc reach, power, and mounts before install day
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a second truck roll to move a termination or find an outlet the first visit assumed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Obtain written landlord consent and verify the permit class before the order commits dates
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a stranded antenna design and a burned install date when the roof is denied after ordering

anti_rework_rules.rule: Map bundled services and their addressing dependencies before writing the failover design
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesign and emergency reconfiguration when the payment terminal breaks on the first WAN change

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify the program's agent-of-record identifiers on every order before submission
anti_rework_rules.prevents: months of attribution-correction chasing for activations that posted unattributed

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the failover test plan at design time, not at handoff
anti_rework_rules.prevents: ad-hoc disruptive testing on a live business and untestable survive claims discovered late

anti_rework_rules.rule: Verify delivered service against the order before customer sign-off
anti_rework_rules.prevents: billing disputes and re-provisioning tickets that replay the install after the carrier machinery disengaged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold the old service live as rollback until the new path has carried the trading-critical traffic
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unrecoverable whole-business outage when a cutover surprise has no path back

iteration_protocol.trigger: the failover test fails or surprises (service drops, no damped failback, long switchover)
iteration_protocol.action: send findings back through design and configuration, fix, and re-run the full test before handoff

iteration_protocol.trigger: a FOC slip, jeopardy code, or special-construction notice posts on an open order
iteration_protocol.action: reset customer dates with the mechanism explained, evaluate interim wireless activation, and reassess the pairing if slips become chronic

iteration_protocol.trigger: a re-qual, order rejection, or footprint change contradicts a stored serviceability result
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the qual, rebuild the affected site's option matrix, and update the rollup and scope

iteration_protocol.trigger: activation verification finds a delivered-versus-ordered mismatch
iteration_protocol.action: drive the correction through the open order, re-verify at the demarc, and update the closing record

iteration_protocol.trigger: the carrier revises program rules, the ordering portal, or the identifier scheme
iteration_protocol.action: re-verify the affected commitments, update order assembly practice, and re-check any in-flight orders

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new bundled service is sold or discovered at an activated site
iteration_protocol.action: re-map dependencies, revise the survive/shed policy, and re-test failover with the new service exercised

iteration_protocol.trigger: post-activation reports show backup underperformance or a real outage diverging from the test record
iteration_protocol.action: re-measure signal at the site, adjust placement or antenna, and re-run the failover test to a new record
